events.comment: Samurai_Boss: every Samurai rule, shared by Samurai_Fight and Tutorial_Level. The scene links Player_Movement and Combat_Shared before this sheet. Tutorial_Level sets his Lives, UltMaxCasts and DebugInactive at scene start, before its link to this sheet.
Scene start: set the Samurai's walk speed and start his timers.

Samurai: keep his HP bar 3px above his head. Row 47 is the top of his head in the 96px frames, and his origin is at row 52.5, so the bar stays still between frames. The posture bar is fixed at the top of the screen.
Samurai: stay idle once the player is deleted.

Samurai: posture broke, so cancel its attack, including any wall slash or dash strike that has not landed yet. Cuts that are already out (a Quickdraw, the mirror's paired cuts) are removed too: a stunned Samurai does not finish his attack.
Samurai: stun ended or deathblow landed, so go back to chasing.

Samurai: a lunge landed, so cancel whatever he is doing and flinch. A posture break, lost life or death from the same hit takes priority. Not during a grab: it has hyperarmor (a hit does not interrupt it).
Samurai: the stagger ended, so go back to chasing.
Debug inactive (key 0): a stagger or stun just ended and sent him back to chasing, so stand idle again instead.
Samurai: count deflects during his swing combo. The third one plays the sword clash on top of the parry sound.
Third deflect of the combo: play the clash and start counting again.
Samurai recoil after a lunge stagger: slide away from the player for RecoilTime seconds, at RecoilSpeed.
Player on the right: slide left.
Player on the left: slide right.
Samurai: play its hit sound when it hits the player.
Stun: pause on the kneeling frame.
Stun: after KneelHold seconds, play the get-up frames.
Boss: final death. Play Samurai_Death, with two holds handled below, and leave the body on its last frame. Petals still out pop.
Death: pause on the settled kneeling frame, before he reaches for the blade.
Death: after DeathKneelHold seconds, carry on with the seppuku.
Death: pause with the blade drawn in, before he collapses.
Death: after DeathCutHold seconds, play the collapse.

Debug, Delete: he loses a life right now (Lives down by one, full HP), which starts the intermission into the next phase: the single cuts into phase 2, the three sets into phase 3 (only on his last life, in the fight scene). Ignored during a stun, death, intermission, ultimate or grab. Remove before release (DEBUG_KEYS).

Boss: lost a life, so start the intermission. Physics stay off during the taller petal animations, so the boss does not jump upward. Any petals still out pop. His bars stay up through it. Into phase 3 the bar stays up but empty (BarMode 1): he is 'dead' for the card.

Boss: at 75%, 50% and 25% HP on the last life (UltHpStep 25, UltMaxCasts 3), cast the ultimate. A hit that crosses two marks only triggers one cast. Locks the player, removes attacks still in flight, and starts the petal teleport instead of the cut. His bars stay up through it.
Grab hyperarmor: a dodge that was already decided (WillDodgeHit) is dropped the moment a grab starts, so a swing while he grabs cannot turn the grab into a dodge.

Boss: dodged a hit. The first dodge of the fight always goes behind the player, later ones are random. Every dodge leaves an image behind (DodgeImgPending): see the dodge image events at the end of the sheet.
Dodge chance by phase: DodgeChanceP1, P2 and P3 (10, 20 and 40) become DodgeChance, which the two dodge checks below read (each phase from its number up overrides the one before).

Boss: the player swings nearby, so maybe dodge that hit. DodgeChance and DodgeDelay control this. He cannot dodge during a stagger, while sheathing after a grab, during the petal cast, or while inactive from the debug key. Not during a grab (GrabTell, GrabReach, GrabHold, GrabWhiff): the grab has hyperarmor.
Boss: a lunge is coming in, so check once per lunge whether to dodge it. It starts too far away for the check above, which only runs on an attack press.
Same rules as a swing: DodgeChance and DodgeDelay control this, and no dodge during the petal cast or while inactive.
Boss offense: every GrabCooldown seconds, with the player within GrabTriggerRange, start a grab. GrabCount alternates the stab and the back stab.
Boss offense, phase 1: every PetalCooldown seconds, with the player at least PetalMinRange away, cast the petals. Skipped while petals from the last cast are still out.
Phase 1: PetalCountP1 petals over an arc of PetalArcP1 degrees above the player.
Phase 2: PetalCountP2 petals over an arc of PetalArcP2 degrees, a half circle around the player (the fight scene: 5 petals, 180 degrees).
Phase 3: PetalCountP3 petals (10, double the five of phase 2) over an arc of PetalArcP3 degrees, a half circle around the player; they launch 35% faster so the volley does not take too long.
Player on the right: face right for the cast.
Player on the left: face left.

Grab timing: the cooldown timer is held at zero until the fight has really started (the opening kneel, rise and bow, or waiting), so the first grab comes GrabCooldownNow seconds into the fight instead of right away. After each grab the next one waits a random GrabCooldownMin to GrabCooldownMax seconds.
Every second grab is the back stab: he flash-steps to land in front of the player, facing them.

Boss offense: when the cooldown is ready and the player is far away, roll a new cooldown. On a successful roll, flash the eye glint before the dash strike. Otherwise keep walking. Not within 1.5 s of the skill timer restarting (a skill or a dash just ended), so two dashes never come back to back.
Boss offense: the eye glint finished, so start the dash strike.

Melee window (phases 2 and 3): when his skill timer is up, MeleeChance % of the time he skips the skill and fights in melee instead for one more SkillDelay: he keeps walking in and swings his combo, so deflecting matters and builds posture. MeleePhase 1 means that window is on.
Melee window over: the next skill is allowed again (and a melee window cannot be rolled twice in a row: this frame's roll above already ran).
Aggressive phase, player at range: choose a skill.

Forced skill: after a crossing attack ForceSkill is 1, so at the next AggroReady (player far, or close: then he dashes away first) he uses a skill straight away, whatever the skill timer says. This is what stops him chaining crossing after crossing in melee range.
Aggressive phase, player close: dash away, then choose a skill.
Aggressive phase: pick a Judgement Cut, the tornado or the petals at random. The petals have a cooldown (PetalCooldown) here too. Two skills in a row without a tornado guarantee a tornado next.
Variety: the same skill is not picked twice in a row (LastSkill). The guards below (petals still out, petal cooldown, a tornado after two skills) may still change the pick.
Petals rolled while petals from the last cast are still out: use a Judgement Cut instead.
Petals rolled within PetalCooldown seconds of the last cast (the timer restarts when a cast ends): use a Judgement Cut instead, so the petal cast cannot come back to back.
Phase 3: with MirrorChance % a Judgement Cut or a petal cast is the mirror version (the mirror image joins him). UseMirror remembers the roll.
Mirror Judgement Cut: he dashes a little way from the player, the mirror appears behind him, and both cast at once.
Mirror petal waves: he and the mirror cast their petals together, in three waves.
Combo: sometimes go to the far wall first, then cast the tornado and follow it with a dash.
Petals: cast them on the player.
Phase 1: PetalCountP1 petals over an arc of PetalArcP1 degrees above the player.
Phase 2: PetalCountP2 petals over an arc of PetalArcP2 degrees, a half circle around the player (the fight scene: 5 petals, 180 degrees).
Phase 3: PetalCountP3 petals (10, double the five of phase 2) over an arc of PetalArcP3 degrees, a half circle around the player; they launch 35% faster so the volley does not take too long.
Player on the right: face right for the cast.
Player on the left: face left.
Remember the pick for the variety rule above.

Flash step: halfway through vanishing, teleport and draw the trail, then face the player. The dash strike passes through the player and faces away. If a wall leaves no room, it lands in front and uses the crescent slash.
Back stab: land in front of the player, GrabPassStart away, for the tell.
Back stab: the player was caught, so land on their far side, GrabPassHold away.
Back stab finished: dash GrabPassExit away from the player, which hides the sheathe.
Grab: land close behind the player, on the side they are not facing.
Back stab: he lands facing away from the player, with the sword under his arm pointing at them.

Flash step finished: counter after going behind. After a dash away in the aggressive phase, choose a skill. After the combo dash, cast the tornado. Landing also restarts the dodge timer, so a dash away cannot be followed at once by another dodge.

A dodge leaves an image where he stood (DashFromX), but only in phase 3, and only when he has LANDED (not at the teleport, which was too quick): it faces the player, holds its sword up for DodgeImgTell seconds, lunges, swings. The dodge image events at the end of the sheet take it from here. Phases 1 and 2 dodge without an image. Only one at a time, and none when he is stunned.

Second image of a chained double dodge: he has landed from the second dash, so the second image appears where he stood (the first landing spot). The first image, which has been holding its sword, is released (DodgeChainWait 0) and swings first; this one swings right after it.

Dodge chain (phase 3, DodgeChainChance %, once per dodge): right after the first image appears he dashes away again, at once, leaving a second image where he lands next. The first image holds its sword until then (DodgeChainWait). The order is: dash, image, dash, first image swings, second image swings, he carries on.
Grab: he has landed. Show the warning kanji over his head and start the tell, with the eye glint.
Back stab: he has landed behind the caught player, so stab. They are turned to face away from him, so the blade goes in through their back.
Back stab: the exit dash has landed. Wait in GrabRecover until the player is back up.

Dodge image waiting: if the dodge left an image, he stands and waits (DodgeWait) until the image has swung (DodgeImgState 5 or 0), so his own attack or skill never comes on top of it. Without an image (phases 1 and 2) he carries on as before.
Grab tell: he can be hit here, and a posture break cancels the grab. Keep the kanji over his head and keep facing the player.
Keep the warning kanji centered above his head while it exists.
Remove the kanji if the grab was interrupted, by a stun, dodge, ultimate or debug key.
Grab tell over: one hand leaves the hilt and reaches for the player. Only a dodge or distance beats this, because the grab skips the deflect check.

Grab connects: the player is within GrabRange and not rolling or invulnerable. He seizes them, and they stand frozen in the idle pose until the blade goes in. For the back stab, the player is caught here and the flash-through follows.
Turn the player to face him, so they fall away from him.
Back stab: the player is caught, so flash through them. If a wall leaves no room behind them, this stays a normal stab.
Grab missed: he is left over-reached for GrabWhiffTime seconds, which is the punish window.
Grab missed: recover and go back to chasing.
Grab: he steps in to GrabHoldNow from the player before the stab, so the player is never pulled toward him.

parameters: (Player.CenterX() + sign(Samurai_NPC.CenterX() - Player.CenterX()) * Samurai_NPC.Variable(GrabHoldNow) - Samurai_NPC.CenterX()) * min(1, 25 * TimeDelta())

events.comment: Grab: the blade goes in. GrabDamage applies directly here, so the deflect check never sees it. The HP can be rallied back like any other hit.
The player only reacts now, as the blade goes in. Frame 4 of Player_Grabbed is the frame that matches the stab.
Grab: he rips the blade out.
Grab: the player hits the ground.
Back stab: the blade is out, so dash away. The player keeps falling, and the dash hides the sheathe.

Grab over: the player has got up, so free them. He may still be sheathing, or already gone after a back stab. From the normal stab, GrabRecover lets the sheathe finish. He can be hit during it, which makes it a small punish window.
He is still at the player, so let him finish.
Grab recovery: the sheathe has finished and the player is up, so go back to chasing.
Wall slash: the boss can be hit once the arrival streak ends. The stance and sword glint are the punish window.
Dash strike: spawn a hidden hitbox covering only the slash line, not his body.
Wall slash: spawn a hidden hitbox covering only the crescent, on the frames where it appears.
Dash strike finished: go back to chasing and start the dash cooldown and the skill timer from now, so no dash skill (the tornado combo, the mirror tornado) follows straight away.
Wall slash finished: go back to chasing and start the dash cooldown and the skill timer from now, so no dash skill (the tornado combo, the mirror tornado) follows straight away.
Dash strike: remove the line hitbox once the slash has faded.
Wall slash: remove the crescent hitbox when the crescent fades.
Dash strike and wall slash: remove the hidden hitbox if the attack was interrupted.

Quickdraw: on the draw frame, cut at the player position with a random variation, and play the Judgement Cut sound. Two in every three Quickdraws are triples (below): single, triple, triple, single, ...
Debug Shift+F2: DebugTriple forces this draw to be a triple in any phase (the normal triple is phase 3 only). It is cleared as it is used.

Triple Judgement Cut, phase 3 only (phases 1 and 2 cast single cuts): two in every three Quickdraws (all but the 1st, 4th, 7th, ...) cast TripleCuts cuts instead of one: this one on the player, then one to its left and one to its right. He holds his draw pose while the other two come out, TripleGap seconds apart.

Triple Judgement Cut: every TripleGap seconds, the next cut appears beside the first one: first to its left, then to its right. Each overlaps the middle cut by TripleOverlap (15%) of its width, so the three cover about 2.7 cuts' width and cannot be outrun. They are placed from where the player stood at the first cast (TripleX, TripleY), each with its own sound. A posture break or any change of state ends the Quickdraw, so the rest are cancelled.

parameters: Samurai_NPC.Variable(TripleX) + (1 - 2 * Samurai_NPC.Variable(TripleLeft)) * (1 - Samurai_NPC.Variable(TripleOverlap)) * Samurai_NPC.Variable(CutCirclePx) * Samurai_NPC.ScaleX() * Samurai_NPC.Variable(CutSizeMul)

events.comment: Last cut out: he finishes the Quickdraw animation, and the Quickdraw ends as usual.
Quickdraw finished: go back to chasing.

Mirror Judgement Cut, setup: he faces the player, picks the way away from them, and starts a short dash (MirrorDashTime seconds at MirrorDashSpeed, not across the arena: the player can catch up and hit him). He can be hit during it.
Dash away: the way he is from the player.
Player on his right side: the dash goes left.
Player on the right: face right.
Player on the left: face left.

Mirror Judgement Cut, the dash: slide away for MirrorDashTime seconds, kept inside the arena. Then the mirror appears slightly behind him and both start the draw together (frame 3 on, as his Quickdraw does).
Player on the right: face right.
Player on the left: face left.
Player on the right: face right.
Player on the left: face left.
Mirror Judgement Cut, the mirror fades in (MirrorFade is its opacity, up to 200 of 255) while the cut is drawn.

Mirror Judgement Cut, the draw frame: both cast at once, one cut left and one right of the player, MirrorCutSpread of a cut's width from them, so standing still gets hit by both. Both cuts are SharedDeflect 1: one deflect stops both. One sound.
Mirror Judgement Cut: the draw is done, so the mirror starts to fade away.
Mirror Judgement Cut, the fade out: when it is gone, he goes back to chasing and the skill timer restarts.

Mirror petal waves, setup: he faces the player and starts the petal cast; the mirror appears behind him (away from the player) and casts too. PetalCount and PetalArc are the half circle of MirrorPetalCount petals.
The mirror goes behind him: away from the player.
Player on the right: face right.
Player on the left: face left.
Player on the right: face right.
Player on the left: face left.
Mirror petal waves: the mirror fades in over the cast.

Mirror petal waves: on frame PetalSpawnFrame the blade sinks, and MirrorPetalCount petals (5 each for him and the mirror) appear in a half circle around the player, slot 0 on the left. Each slot belongs to a wave (WaveMap: 2, then 3, then 5 petals): a wave launches together (a small ripple across the arc), the next wave WaveGap seconds later. Every petal is SharedDeflect 1 with its wave in WaveId, so one deflect stops the whole wave.
Create one petal per count. They start as "new" and are laid out by the next event.

Lay out each new petal around the player's body, where the player is right now. It stays at that spot. Slot 0 is the leftmost point of the arc above the player. Launches go left to right, PetalGap seconds apart, the first PetalFirstLaunch seconds after the spawn.
Mirror petal waves: hold the open hand (both of them) while the petals wait to launch.
Mirror petal waves: when every petal has launched, both lower the arm.
Each petal still forming, hovering or glinting counts as waiting.
All petals have launched, so lower the arm.
Mirror petal waves: the arm is down, so the mirror starts to fade away and the skill and petal cooldowns start.
Mirror petal waves, the fade out: when it is gone, he goes back to chasing.
Debug, End: the mirror petal waves right now, whatever he was doing. Ignored during a stun, death, intermission, ultimate or grab. Remove before release (DEBUG_KEYS).
Wave deflect: when a petal that belongs to a wave was deflected (the player was not hurt), every other petal of that wave bursts with it, so one deflect handles the whole wave.
Mirror image: its opacity is MirrorFade, every frame.

Mirror image, the glitch starts: a new mirror (GlitchOn 0) is moved onto the Samurai (it appears on top of him) and remembers where it should end up (GlitchTargetX); the next event phases it out to that spot. When it travels 150 px or more it leaves a dash line, like his own flash step.

Mirror image, the glitch: for its first MirrorGlitchTime seconds it flickers (opacity steps between 50%, 80% and 110%, pale cyan, pale magenta and white). For the first MirrorPhaseTime seconds it also phases out of the Samurai to its spawn point (GlitchStartX to GlitchTargetX, easing out), shuddering a little on the way.

parameters: Samurai_Mirror.Variable(GlitchStartX) + (Samurai_Mirror.Variable(GlitchTargetX) - Samurai_Mirror.Variable(GlitchStartX)) * (1 - (1 - min(1, Samurai_Mirror.Variable(GlitchT) / Samurai_NPC.Variable(MirrorPhaseTime))) * (1 - min(1, Samurai_Mirror.Variable(GlitchT) / Samurai_NPC.Variable(MirrorPhaseTime)))) + RandomInRange(-8, 8) * (1 - min(1, Samurai_Mirror.Variable(GlitchT) / Samurai_NPC.Variable(MirrorPhaseTime)))

events.comment: Mirror image, the glitch is over: it sits exactly on its spawn point, with no tint (GlitchOn 2).

Mirror image, shimmer style 0 (MirrorStyle 0): once settled (GlitchOn 2) the whole figure is never quite still, as if overwhelmed with energy. Every 0.07 s it shifts up to 1 px sideways (ShimmerOff, taken back off first) and its tint and opacity wobble very slightly.

Mirror image, shimmer style 1 (MirrorStyle 1, the default): the figure stays still, but its outline never does. Once settled, every 0.1 s the RGB split effect on the mirror (Split) throws its red, green and blue edges 1.2 px or less in random directions, so the contour crawls like static. The fringe is part of the sprite, so it fades together with him.
Mirror image cleanup: it only exists while he is in one of the mirror skills. Anything that interrupts him (a stun, a stagger, a life lost, death) takes it away with him.

Mirror tornado, setup: he vanishes (the flash step's back dash, invulnerable). The ends of the arena are picked: he takes the one away from the player, the mirror the other, so the two never overlap and the player stands between them (MirrorEndNear and MirrorEndFar are the two spots).
Player on the left half: he takes the far right end, the mirror the left.
Player on the right half: the other way round.

Mirror tornado, the teleport: halfway through vanishing he lands at his end with a trail, and the mirror appears at the other end. Both face the way their tornado will go and start the cast from frame 0.
Both face the way their tornado goes: toward the other end of the arena (not toward the player: with the player against a wall the mirror would face the wall).
Mirror tornado: the mirror fades in over the cast.

Mirror tornado, the release frame (20, as the plain tornado): his tornado goes from his end toward the other end, the mirror's from its end the other way, so the two cross the arena towards each other.
The mirror's tornado, in its own event: two Create actions in one event leave both tornadoes picked, and the second one's speed overwrote the first (his tornado went the wrong way).

Mirror tornado, the cast is over. With TornadoComboChance % (or the debug key) the dash strike follows, as in the plain tornado combo, and the mirror joins it (it stays, idle, until the strike starts). Otherwise the mirror fades away.
The dash follows: he flashes the eye glint (DashTell) and the mirror waits for the strike.
Mirror tornado, no dash: the mirror fades out, then he goes back to chasing.

Mirror dash, the strike starts (he has just landed through the player): the mirror lands through the player from its own side, 100 px beyond them, faces away like him and plays the same passing strike.
Mirror: player on its right, so it ends facing away (left).
Mirror: player on its left, so it ends facing away (right).
Mirror dash: its slash line (the same hitbox as his) appears on frame 2 of its strike.
Mirror dash: the strike is over, so the mirror fades away.
Mirror dash, abandoned: if he leaves the dash (a stun, a stagger) the mirror's strike is cancelled and the cleanup removes the mirror.

Debug, Numpad1: the mirror tornado right now (no dash after it). Numpad2: the same with the dash strike after it, both through the player. Ignored during a stun, death, intermission, ultimate or grab. Remove before release (DEBUG_KEYS).
Debug, Insert: jump to phase 2 (his second life, full HP, aggressive). Ignored during a stun, death, intermission, ultimate or grab. Remove before release (DEBUG_KEYS).
Debug, PageUp: jump to phase 3 (his last life, full HP, aggressive, the mirror skills and triple cuts on). Remove before release (DEBUG_KEYS).
Debug, PageDown: a melee window right now (he walks in and swings, no skills) for one SkillDelay. Remove before release (DEBUG_KEYS).

Debug, Home: the mirror Judgement Cut right now (the dash, the mirror, the paired cuts), whatever he was doing. Ignored during a stun, death, intermission, ultimate or grab. Remove before release (DEBUG_KEYS).
Tornado: on the release frame, send it the way the boss is facing (right).
Tornado: on the release frame, send it the way the boss is facing (left).
Tornado cast finished: go back to chasing. In the combo, flash the eye glint and follow up with the dash strike.
Petal cast: on frame PetalSpawnFrame, the blade has sunk into the ground, so create PetalCount petals at the player. Each one then waits for its slot below.
Create one petal per count. They start as "new" and are laid out by the next event.

Lay out each new petal around the player's body, where the player is right now. It stays at that spot. Slot 0 is the leftmost point of the arc above the player. Launches go left to right, PetalGap seconds apart, the first PetalFirstLaunch seconds after the spawn.
Petal cast: hold the open hand on frame PetalHoldFrame while the petals are waiting to launch. He does nothing else here and can be hit.
Petal cast hold: count the petals that have not launched yet. Any that burst early, for example on a deflect, no longer count.
Each petal still forming, hovering or glinting counts as waiting.
All petals have launched, so lower the arm.
Petal cast finished: go back to chasing, and start the skill and petal cooldowns from now.
Intermission: the petal burst ended, so hide and start the cuts.
Into phase 2 (his second life, in the fight scene): three sets of cuts instead of single ones. CutsLeft counts the sets.

Into phase 3 (his last life, in the fight scene): no cuts. The true form: the bar stays up, empty (BarMode 1, he is 'dead'), the ENEMY DEFEATED card comes up (CardState 1), and the steps below (IntermissionStep 4 to 6) run it.

Intermission into phase 3, a set starts: when the last set's cuts are gone, SweepSetGap seconds after, the next set starts where the player stands now. Three sets: (1) triple cuts sweeping right to left starting at the player, (2) sweeping left to right, (3) one cut straight on the player, then the two side cuts right after.
Set 1: three cuts sweep from the player to the left, SweepGap seconds apart (each a cut's width, overlapped like the triple cut).

parameters: clamp(Samurai_NPC.Variable(SweepX) - Samurai_NPC.Variable(SweepStep) * Samurai_NPC.Variable(CutCirclePx) * Samurai_NPC.ScaleX() * Samurai_NPC.Variable(CutSizeMul) * (1 - Samurai_NPC.Variable(TripleOverlap)), 60, 1220)

events.comment: Set 2: three cuts sweep from the left of the player to the right.
Set 3, the first cut: straight on top of the player.
Set 3, right after (SweepGap seconds): the two side cuts, both at once.
Intermission into phase 3, a set is done (set 1 and 2: three cuts out; set 3: the centre and the two sides): the gap before the next set starts.
Intermission: launch a cut at the player every 1.8 seconds, with the Judgement Cut sound. Each cut takes 1.7 seconds, so they do not overlap.
Intermission: all cuts finished, so reappear on the far side and switch to the aggressive phase.
Intermission finished: switch back to a normal-height animation, turn platformer physics back on, and start chasing.
True form, the card is up (IntermissionStep 4): after CardHold seconds the card is slashed in half (CardState 2), with his normal attack sound (it lands with the white flash).

True form, the slash (step 5): after CardSlashTime seconds the card is gone, and he appears on the far side from the player, gathering out of petals, with his bar filling back up and its name changing (BarMode 2). Then the normal end of the intermission (step 3) takes over: he is back in the fight, with no Thousand Cuts until 75%, 50% and 25%.
Ultimate teleport: the Samurai has dissolved into petals, so the player does too, with their own animation. IsGrabbed keeps a deflect press or stray hit from replacing it until they reform.
Ultimate teleport: both are gone, so move them to mid-arena. The Samurai keeps the side he was on, UltStandoff away from the player. UltCenterX is the arena middle.
Ultimate teleport: start the player reforming, so both finish together.
Ultimate teleport: both have reformed, so give the player control of their deflect, bring back the bars, turn physics back on, and start the draw.
Ultimate: on the draw frame, cast Thousand Cuts on the player. The first slash lands on frame 13, and the rest follow every 3 frames.
Ultimate tell: on frame UltTellFrame, 0.32 seconds before the first slash, flash the gold kanji over the player with a sharp ring. Gold means it can be deflected, red means it cannot.
Ultimate tell: the first slash has landed, so remove the kanji.
Ultimate finished: unlock the player and go back to the aggressive phase.
Ultimate: allow a new hit between slashes. Slashes land on frames 13, 16, 19, 22, 25, 28, 31, and 34. Uses mod() because GDevelop expressions have no % operator.
Move the tornado along the ground.
Tornado: loop its full-size frames while it crosses the arena.
Tornado: near the left edge, start the fade so it finishes at the wall.
Tornado: near the right edge, start the fade so it finishes at the wall.

Judgement Cut timing: each cut's frames follow judgement_cut.wav instead of a fixed speed. The circle appears on the boom and holds, the slash lines land on the sound's slashes, and the burst (frames 12 and 13, the only frames with a full hitbox) comes with the last slash at 1.40 s, so the cut hits once there. It then shatters and is removed at 1.70 s. Edit FRAMES to retime it.

inlineCode: // Judgement Cut timing, synced to judgement_cut.wav. Frame k shows from FRAMES[k] seconds after the cut appears.
const END = 1.7; // Seconds: the cut is removed here.

events.comment: Remove a Judgement Cut when its animation ends.
Remove the tornado when its animation ends.

Petals: until launch, stay in place and keep the tip pointing at the middle of the player's body. That is 77% down the player's frame, the middle of their collision mask (rows 43 to 80 of 80), the same in every animation. CenterY() would be the top of the head.
Petals: formed, so hover.
Petals: PetalGlintTime seconds before launch, the edge glints red. This is the tell for each petal.

Petals: while the edge glints (the last PetalGlintTime seconds before launch), the petal draws back away from the player at PetalPullSpeed, the wind-up, and then launches fast from there. Its tip keeps pointing at the player, so backing off is straight along its aim.
Petals: launch at LaunchAt, along the direction the petal points, which is at where the player is right now. It flies straight from here and stops tracking.
Petals: fly in a straight line, with momentum: they start slow after the draw-back and build up to full speed over PetalAccelTime seconds (Mom goes 0 to 1; the speed is 15% + 85% of Mom squared).
Petals: hit the player or deflected, so burst. Combat_Shared sets HasHit for both.
Petals: missed and reached the ground or a wall, so burst there.
Petals: safety net. Burst any petal still flying 3 seconds after its launch time.
Petals: the player is gone, so burst every petal that is still out.

Petals: a bursting petal comes apart into blossom petals. Create the pop where it was, at the same size and never rotated, so the petals always drift and sink downward, then remove the blade. One at a time, so two bursting on the same frame both get a pop.

events.comment: Dash trails fade out in steps over their 0.2 s life (every dash line: the flash steps, the mirror glitch and the crossing image's lunge).
Remove the dash trail after 0.2 seconds.

Boss bar, dead: while BarMode is 1 the HP bar is drawn empty, though his HP variable is not touched (a real 0 would count as his death in Combat_Shared). BarMode 2: it fills back up over 1.2 s (BarFill), then it follows his HP again.
Phase 3 speed: from phase 3 on he chases at RunSpeedP3 instead of RunSpeed, in the run animation. Set every frame, so the debug jumps (PageUp) get it too.
Afterimages, anchor: whenever he is not chasing, LastImageX follows him, so the first image after a dash or a skill is not left a whole arena away.

Afterimages (phase 3 speed technique): while he chases in phase 3, a still copy of his run frame is left behind every AfterimageGap px of travel (at most 22 at once). It uses his current frame and facing, a pale cool tint and AfterimageOpacity, sits behind him, never moves and never attacks (it has no hitbox and no behaviour).
Afterimages fade: each loses opacity at AfterimageFadeRate per second and is removed at zero.

Debug, Num1 (top row): the old back dash, right now: old speeds (DashFast 0, mirror dash 520 px/s for 0.3 s) and he cancels what he is doing and flash-steps away. Num2: the same with the faster ones (DashFast 1, 20% faster: animation speed 1.2, mirror dash 624 px/s for 0.25 s). Faster is the default. Ignored during a stun, death, intermission, ultimate or grab. Remove before release (DEBUG_KEYS).

Back dash speed: his animation runs at normal speed except in a back dash (the flash step away, and the one before the tornado combo and the mirror tornado), where it runs 20% faster when DashFast is 1.

Directional deflecting, the Samurai's part (the rule itself is in Combat_Shared): DeflectAnySide is 1, so a deflect works whichever way the player faces, during the intermission and at his death. The mirror image does not count as a second boss: the direction is always toward the real Samurai, so the mirror's attacks only need the player to face him. The Judgement Cut, the Thousand Cuts and the petals have Directional 0 (any side).
Crossing attacks enabled: only in a scene with a third phase (the fight), and from phase 2.

Directional deflecting, whose attack it is: AimX is -1 (the boss himself) except while the crossing illusion swings (CrossMirrorDone 0 or 1, with an illusion): then it is the illusion's x, so the player has to face the illusion for that swing.
undefined The dodge image's swing works the same way (DodgeImgState 4).

Crossing attack, landing (step 6): he has flash-stepped to the other side of the player and raises his swing (the Samurai_Attack animation, held on frame 3). With CrossUseMirror 1 the image he left behind (at DashFromX) appears at once, in its own look (the mirror sprites) and facing the player from where it stands, and raises its swing too. CrossTimer starts: the image swings after CrossMirrorAt seconds and he after CrossSamAt, so the player has the gap between to turn; with no image he swings after CrossSoloAt. In phase 3 the image then lunges at the player (the CrossImg events below) before it swings. CrossImgSide remembers which side of him it spawned on.
Crossing attack: until it swings, each figure keeps turning toward the player from where it stands.
Crossing attack: hold each raised sword on frame 3 until its release.
Crossing attack, the image's swing: once its lunge has ended (CrossImgDash 2), its hitbox at its own sword point. He swings CrossSamGap seconds after it (and not before CrossSamAt).

Crossing image, the lunge starts (step 1): after CrossMirrorAt seconds of telegraph (it stands with the sword raised, held on frame 3) it dashes at the player. The dash is harmless: only the swing at the end has a hitbox (the dash is a lunge, not a hit).

Crossing image, the lunge (step 2): speed builds by CrossImgAccel px/s2 up to CrossImgSpeed px/s, toward where the player is now. It stops CrossImgRange px short of them. Spawn-side lock: it can never get closer than CrossImgMinGap px to him on the side it spawned on (CrossImgSide), so it never crosses him or overlaps his hitbox. CrossImgDelta is the move this frame.

events.comment: Crossing image, the lunge leaves a dash line: each frame a line piece from where it was to where it is, with a 60 px tail behind it. The pieces fade out (the fade events by the dash trail removal).

Crossing image, the lunge ends (step 3), whichever comes first, and the swing follows: it is within CrossImgRange of the player; CrossImgMaxTime seconds have passed; it has gone CrossImgMaxDist px (the player ran off); or the side lock stopped it (it moved less than half a pixel at speed). Separate events, not an Or.
Crossing attack, his swing: CrossSamAt seconds after landing when the image swings first, CrossSoloAt when he is alone.
Crossing attack: the image's swing is over, so its hitbox goes (his own swing is not out yet).
Crossing attack: his swing is over, so its hitbox goes. One step of the sequence is done (CrossLegsLeft counts the steps still to come).
Crossing attack, step 8: the image fades (or, with none, straight on).

Crossing attack, step 9: with a step still to come he flash-steps back across the player; otherwise he rests for a moment (the Cooldown state) before the next move. He no longer restarts the skill timer here (that made him swing crossing after crossing while the player stayed in melee range): ForceSkill 1 makes the next skill come at once, in phases 2 and 3.

Samurai_AggroReady Rules
Close enough: start attacking. AttackRange is the same distance the follow-up check uses after each swing.
Samurai_Attacking Rules
First swing of a combo: start the deflect count over.
Swing: hold the raised sword for SwingPause seconds. The wait is the same every swing, so the rhythm can be learned.
Swing: after SwingPause seconds, release the sword and create the hitbox.

Swing finished, combo not over: if the player is behind the samurai or out of AttackRange, skip the next swing and go back to AggroReady to close the gap. ComboCount is kept, so the 3-swing limit still leads to Cooldown.

The crossing attacks, after the first swing instead of swings two and three (CrossEnabled: the fight scene, from phase 2 on; the Tutorial keeps the old combo). He flash-steps to the far side of the player (DashType cross) and swings; with CrossLegsLeft 2 he then steps back and swings again (front, behind, back). In phase 3 (CrossUseMirror 1) the image he leaves behind at each step swings too. Phase 3 rolls one or two legs (Cross2Split). CrossForce is the debug keys Num3 to Num5.

events.comment: DODGE IMAGE. Every dodge (phases 1 to 3) leaves an image of him where he stood (Samurai_DodgeImage, the mirror look, never hurt by anything). It does what the crossing image does: holds its sword up for CrossMirrorAt seconds, lunges at the player (harmless; the CrossImg tuning variables are shared), swings, and he does not have to wait for it. DodgeImgState: 0 none, 1 telegraph, 2 lunge, 3 swing starts, 4 swinging, 5 fading.
Dodge image: until it swings it keeps turning toward the player, and holds its raised sword on frame 3.

Dodge image, the lunge starts after DodgeImgTell seconds of telegraph, counted from his landing. In a chained double dodge the first image keeps holding (DodgeChainWait) until the second image has appeared.

Dodge image, the lunge: the same maths as the crossing image (CrossImgSpeed, CrossImgAccel, CrossImgRange, CrossImgMinGap, CrossImgSide replaced by DodgeImgSide: it stays on its side of him), and a fading dash line.
